jobs.description: Reflect each new Gold snapshot of gold.unit_price (root ADR-0190) in R2 by-PNU serving (scripts/ops/by-pnu-serving-bake.sh unit-price), as section packs: a change set decides a create-only patch, a reflect-only manifest or a full new generation, as every lane does. Its own job and asset since root ADR-0333, out of `by_pnu_serving_bake all`, where it waited behind the parcel lane (a 20-hour national re-bake on 2026-10-23..28). Its documents follow the building lane's (documents_follow_lane): it bakes a unit price Gold only once the building lane serves a building Gold built from the same register snapshots, and otherwise ends `waiting` until it does, a state the asset reconciler (asset_reconcile) re-checks every five minutes, not a run order inside one unit. Started when gold_unit_price_rebuild commits a new snapshot, by the reconciler when that event was lost or the building lane caught up, and at 10:55 as the fallback (root ADR-0171), apart from the 10:15 and 10:45 bakes so no two clock starts crowd the host at once; each run's containers are its own one-offs (tools/semgrep/rules/batch-containers.yml). One slot and MemoryMax=3G (root ADR-0138): its whole generation is 169,117 documents in nine shards, and with the parcel and public-auction bakes beside it the pool holds 22g, no more than the release builder.

assets.title: 호 공시가격 by-PNU 묶음 파일
assets.description: gold.unit_price 의 PNU 문서를 법정동 묶음 파일로 굽는다. 객체 레인 없이 묶음으로만 서빙하는 첫 레인이다(루트 ADR-0190). 웹은 건물 문서와 호 id 로 합친다.

unit-price.pack_only_reason: a lane of one kind of data (root ADR-0190) is born serving from section packs: it never had an object lane, so its first publish is the pack-only cut-over gate and its Worker never reads objects

document_key_suffix.reason: root ADR-0204: a PNU's unit price document was up to 596 KB gzip (a large apartment complex is one PNU), over the 256 KiB whole-read bound; a document is one building of one PNU (the building's catalog id, the nil UUID for units linked to no building), at most about 148 KB measured. The key is the PNU then the suffix (format 2 packs); the request path is <prefix><pnu>/<suffix>

unit-price.latency_baseline_lane_reason: every PNU with a priced unit has a building document (a unit price is served under the PNU its building document carries it), so the building preview reads the same PNUs through the same Worker code at the same placement: the pack-only gate (나) holds this lane's cold and warm reads to the bounds it holds a cut-over to
unit-price.documents_follow_lane_reason: a unit's price is served under the PNU its building document carries it, and the Gold rebuild places the units of both panels from the same register snapshots (gold-panel-rebuild.contract.json pins_from). This lane bakes in its own job (by_pnu_unit_price_bake, root ADR-0333) and only a Gold built from the same register snapshots as the building Gold the building lane serves (scripts/ops/lane_follow_gate.py); otherwise it waits, so it does not publish units under PNUs the served building documents do not yet carry them under
unit-price.latency_p95_max_ms_reason: the baseline's documents carry more than this lane's (the building document carried the unit price history until root ADR-0190), so a slow building read could hide a slow lane inside the increase bound. Gate (나) also holds this lane's own cold and warm p95 to an absolute bound: the slowest cold pack p95 a lane now serves measured at its cut-over (parcel generation 1, 1,379 ms from ai-server, root ADR-0162)
unit-price.placement_reason: the bucket's location is APAC and the Worker reads it on every cold answer, while this zone's Korean traffic enters at LAX. Measured 2026-10-06 from ai-server, 1,000 PNUs per run, live copy and preview at the same placement: an R2 read of an object read before takes ~190 ms run at LAX, ~40 ms at Tokyo (aws:ap-northeast-1), ~70 ms at Seoul (aws:ap-northeast-2) and ~120 ms at Singapore (aws:ap-southeast-1). At Tokyo a cold pack answer is within the cut-over bounds of the object path (ADR-0154); the object path's own edge-cache hits pay the LAX-Tokyo hop (warm p50 444 -> 553 ms), which is what makes the pack path's edge copies affordable to drop. Placement travels with the uploaded version (2026-10-06, a throwaway Worker split 50/50 between an unplaced version and one uploaded with this hint answered both unplaced and remote-NRT), so the canary's code phase rolls it out and back like any other change
unit-price.cpu_limit_reason: the account is on Workers Paid (2026-10-06), whose default CPU limit is 30 s per request; an explicit limit keeps a runaway request from billing seconds of CPU. 50 ms is five times the cut-over gate's CPU p99 bound (worker_cpu_p99_max_ms) and above every measured path: the object path runs at CPU p50 1.95 ms, the pack path passes the gzip member through, and the decompressing path for a client without gzip does one gunzip and no parse, a subset of the old four-section join that measured CPU p99 37.5 ms

canary.reason: Cloudflare gradual deployments split by request; a step holds 15 minutes, then needs min_requests_per_step pinned reads answered by the new version itself (each answer names the version that served it in version_header) before its error rate, CPU and wall time are compared with the old one
canary.analytics_min_coverage_reason: Workers analytics (workersInvocationsAdaptive) is sampled and late: its sum of requests is already scaled by the sample interval, but on 2026-10-06 it had counted 137 of the 300 pinned reads the new version answered (old version: 296 of 300) when the gate's ten-minute wait ran out, and 304 once the late rows arrived. So whether reads reached the new version is judged from the pinned answers, and analytics is used only for CPU, cut-offs and errors, which a sample answers; it must still have counted this share of the new version's pinned answers, so an analytics answer about the wrong version or window cannot pass as clean

synthetic_load.reason: before launch the live hostname carries a few requests an hour, so 1% of real traffic never reaches min_requests_per_step (it would take about 20,000 live requests in a 15-minute hold). Each step therefore reads 300 gate-sample PNUs from the live hostname at each of the two versions, pinned with Cloudflare's Cloudflare-Workers-Version-Overrides header (honoured only for a version in the current deployment), counts the answers that name the new version in version_header (a misdirected pin shows up as too few of them), and judges each version on its own answers (every one 200 and gzip) as well as on analytics. The PNUs are drawn by the new version id (load::canary_draw): with one fixed draw every rollout read the PNUs earlier runs had left in the old version's edge copies while the new version read them from R2, and on 2026-10-07 the 1% step refused a healthy version on CPU, cold against warm

monitor.reason: hourly (infra/systemd/foundation-by-pnu-serving-monitor@.timer, instance unit-price, switched on by the operator's monitor-sample step right after the lane's first publish), 20 PNUs from the gate sample read from the live hostname and held to the documents the lane's packs hold; the lane has no object documents (root ADR-0190): a 5xx, a document that differs from its packs, or a p95 above what the ai-server-to-edge path shows on a good hour (2026-10-05: about 1-3 s) is an alert
